summary: Montezuma County wooden tower built in the 1930s and now taken down; the register and Colorado list give coordinates several km apart, and no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower has been taken down; the Colorado list marks it Removed; no removal date given

events.note: Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 18, 2009

evidence.supports: Unique wooden tower, built in the 1930s, now taken down
evidence.quote: This unique wooden tower was built in the 1930s and has been taken down.

evidence.supports: Administered by the U.S. Forest Service
Registry number US 535, CO 7 on the register page
Colorado list: Tower, Removed, FFLOS US 535, CO 7
Colorado list coordinates, several km south of the register point

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 37.533000 N, 108.547000 W; the Colorado list gives 37.47791 N, 108.54572 W, several km further south. The story reports both; the sources do not settle which is right.

sources.title: Eagles Nest (McPhee) Tower Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Both sources give only the 1930s for construction, so the events list has no build entry (the schema needs a year); add one once a dated source is found. The brief elevation (2202.8 m) matches the register's 2,203 m; the brief coordinates match the register, not the Colorado list. The brief says this record shares a register number; both sources give US 535 / CO 7 only for this site, and no second site with that number turned up. Search summaries (not used): a USFS assessment, Administering the National Forests of Colorado, Table 5, suggesting a CCC F-53-C Lone Dome crew, and a local researcher's topo-map pin. Neither text was in the cached npshistory inventory pages 1-8, and the firelookout.org eagles page returns 404 in the cache, so both are left out. The CCC attribution is a worthwhile lead to check.
